shorts.title: Obama: Trump's White House looks like "Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Obama's Cheesecake Factory line vs. Trump
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Barack Obama, at a Michigan rally: "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory." [beat] Friends, the review is in. [incredulous] And Trump fired back on Monday: "I would try and explain that to a guy like Obama, but he wouldn't understand." [sarcastic] Understand what? The gold? The ballroom? The helipad? He says the White House "has to be pristine" and is "now in better shape than it was in 1792." [beat] Well, in 1792 it had no ballroom, no gold, and no thirty-page menu. Pristine is doing a lot of work there. [amused] The Federalist, number 51, says "Ambition must be made to counteract ambition." [beat] Nobody told the president that applies to drapes. So, people: is it a renovation, or an appetizer menu with a gift shop? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Grand jury refuses to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, Trump's Jan. 6 witness #Shorts
shorts.hook: A grand jury just told DOJ: no
shorts.narration: [serious] Federal prosecutors wanted an indictment of Cassidy Hutchinson, the former White House aide who testified about January 6. [beat] The grand jury said no. CBS News reports that four sources briefed on the proceedings say it declined. [deadpan] Media reports say House Republican allies of the president made the referral. The Justice Department hadn't responded to CBS. [beat] So let's recap. Trump's allies send a critic to the Justice Department, and a room of ordinary citizens looks at the evidence and says, thanks, we'll pass. [sarcastic] Federalist 47 warns that power piled into the same hands is "the very definition of tyranny." [beat] A grand jury is the opposite: ordinary citizens with no bumper stickers and no Truth Social account. So here's my question, friends: is this Justice, or just payback with a letterhead? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: A grand jury declined to indict Cassidy Hutchinson over her Jan. 6 testimony, according to four sources briefed on the proceedings.
A Justice Department litigator told a magistrate judge at a Tuesday hearing that the grand jury had not agreed to the proposed indictment.
Media reports say House Republican allies of the president made the referral to DOJ; DOJ had not responded to CBS's request for comment.
Hutchinson was a top aide to chief of staff Mark Meadows and testified in 2022 before the House select committee investigating the Jan. 6 attack.
Federalist No. 47: the accumulation of all powers in the same hands "may justly be pronounced the very definition of tyranny."

shorts.title: Waltz at the UN: "Back up! ... This isn't Havana." #Shorts
shorts.narration: [deadpan] At the United Nations on Tuesday, America's ambassador, Mike Waltz, was speaking when Cuba's foreign minister walked toward his podium. [beat] Waltz's response: "Back up! Back up, Ambassador. Back away! This isn't Havana." [incredulous] Cuba's Bruno Rodríguez answered with a literary classic: "Mr. Waltz is lying yet again." [beat] Friends, this was the annual debate on the Cuba embargo. Diplomacy, at the highest level, sounds like a bouncer at a Sacramento nightclub. [sarcastic] Waltz also said, quote, "This is America, my friend. This is the United Nations." [beat] Which is, technically, in New York. Washington's Farewell Address warned that "A passionate attachment of one nation for another produces a variety of evils." Sir, nobody asked for a podium wrestling match. Is that tough diplomacy, or a viral clip with a flag pin? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: At the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez moved toward the podium while U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz was speaking; the clash came during the annual debate on the U.S. embargo on Cuba.
Waltz said: "Back up! Back up, Ambassador. Back away! This isn't Havana."
Waltz said: "This is America, my friend. This is the United Nations. This isn't your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me."
Rodríguez said: "Mr. Waltz is lying yet again."

shorts.title: Ralph Norman on Trump's Senate pick: "Elections have consequences" #Shorts
shorts.hook: GOP feud: "force" a candidate on voters?
shorts.narration: [deadpan] South Carolina Republicans have a family dinner problem. Congressman Ralph Norman lost the GOP Senate runoff to Senator Darline Graham, and now he says he won't campaign for her. [beat] His text to Fox News: "The voters in S.C. are not buying the argument that everyone has to 'settle' for a candidate." He called it an attempt to "force" a candidate on voters. [incredulous] His closing line: "Elections have consequences." [beat] Funny, that's what we say in November. Trump rallied for Graham, telling voters, "You must vote for Darline and Republicans, and just — you're going to be happy." [sarcastic] Must. Happy. Very free-country energy. Cook shifted the race to "Lean Republican." Washington warned of "the alternate domination of one faction over another." Friends, if your own party won't show up, why should I? MAGA fans, explain it in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.) lost the GOP runoff for South Carolina's open Senate seat to Sen. Darline Graham and says he will not campaign for or with her.
Norman texted Fox News Digital: "The voters in S.C. are not buying the argument that everyone has to 'settle' for a candidate" and spoke of attempts to "force" a candidate on the voters of S.C.
Norman closed his message with: "Elections have consequences."
At a South Carolina rally Trump said: "You must vote for Darline and Republicans, and just — you're going to be happy."
The Cook Political Report moved the race from "Likely Republican" to "Lean Republican."
Washington's Farewell Address: "The alternate domination of one faction over another"

shorts.title: Trump: "We may do another little Epic Fury" — war cost: $47.1B so far #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Trump at a Florida rally, on restarting hostilities with Iran after the midterms: "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree." [beat] Little. [deadpan] Meanwhile, U.S. Central Command estimates the war has cost the military at least forty-seven billion dollars as of mid-October. About twenty-nine billion of that is replacing munitions. In September, Trump wrote that we have "virtually unlimited amounts of Mid to High Grade Ammunition." [beat] Unlimited, but somehow already on the reorder list. The Pentagon's inspector general cites "strategic inventory shortfalls." [serious] The Constitution gives Congress the power "To declare War." It says nothing about announcing sequels at a rally. The administration's supplemental funding request has not passed. Friends, who gets to decide the next chapter? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for the daily news.

claims.text: Trump said at a Florida rally last week, on possibly restarting hostilities after the midterms: "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree."
U.S. Central Command estimates the Iran war has cost the U.S. military at least $47.1 billion as of mid-October, about $29 billion of it for replacing expended munitions.
Trump wrote on Truth Social in early September: "we have virtually unlimited amounts of Mid to High Grade Ammunition, far more than we could ever use."
The Pentagon inspector general said the U.S. faces "strategic inventory shortfalls" from munitions expended; the administration's supplemental military funding request has not passed.
